placement.position_note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-0078). This building does not stand centred on a lot at a typology setback: it stands ON the north face of blk_south_water_franklin, the block's South Water Street frontage, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is 1.50 m back from that lot line, which is the closest line the plat module's own margin allows and is not a measurement of this frontage, and its east wall is fixed by the west wall of recon_1835_blk_south_water_franklin_d4_12, which it shares a party line with. The bearing is the face's own, so the front looks square at South Water Street. The run carries no lateral offset, because a shared party wall is one wall and cannot wander. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, which building it was, and that these particular units stood shoulder to shoulder. What the 1834 South Water Street view supports is the TREATMENT — a continuous working row of party walls rather than detached cottages set back on grass. The treatment is what this placement takes from it, and a run standing on any other face of the town is borrowing it from that one street: the view draws a row, it does not place this row. Standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot, and the side lot lines this row crosses were always conjectural.

siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn from the set on this record's stable key, then advanced so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

occupants.note: SEATED BY THE PLACEMENT POLICY'S PLATTED DEAL (data/reconstruction/1835_platted_seats.json, dealt by T-1613 and carried onto this roof by T-1638; liberties L270 and L276). NO SOURCE PLACES THIS HOUSEHOLD HERE, OR ANYWHERE. Its own record gives a name and no address — no street, no lot and not even a division — so both halves of its band were dealt rather than read, and the lot under this roof is the policy's tradesman_dwellings clause answered on the committed plat: blk_south_water_franklin#04, fronting south_water, a standing roof of family D3 the clause admits. THE SOURCES BELOW CARRY THE NAME AND NOTHING ELSE. The roof's own existence, position and footprint remain conjectural and are unchanged by the seating — it is still a count-unit of the 665-roof programme, adopted rather than raised, so nothing was drawn off the reconstruction order book. The household's id is carried in resident_assignment rather than in this prose, because tools/generate_dooryard_pickets.py admits a lot for a garden on an id appearing HERE and a keeper a policy deal seats is not a measurement of anybody's garden.

citations.citation: "Early Chicago Voter Lists" — the poll list of the first election of the Board of Trustees of the Town of Chicago (10 August 1833), the tax list of the Town of Chicago, 1833, the election returns and poll list of 1834 filed 11 August 1834, and the 1835 poll list. Transcribed from the Illinois Regional Archives Depository originals by Ingrid Latimer Schulz, published in Chicago Genealogist XXV/4 (Summer 1993), and republished by the Genealogy Trails Transcription Team.

transcribes.work: Poll list for the first election of Board of Trustees of the Town of Chicago (10 August 1833)
transcribes.note: 30 entries. Andreas says twenty-eight men voted at this election; the list prints thirty names. T-0542 searched for a count outside Andreas and found none — the Chicago Democrat did not exist until 26 November 1833 and its whole run to August 1835 carries no retrospective count of this poll — so the discrepancy STANDS, with the negative search recorded (claims/town_findings_voter_lists.json v004). On weight the thirty are the enrolments and Andreas's twenty-eight is an 1884 belief-statement ('It is believed') about the number of legal voters; neither count is repaired.

transcribes.work: Tax List of the Town of Chicago - 1833
transcribes.note: 115 entries. Names only — as published it carries no valuation, no lot and no figure, so it is not a ranked property roll (claims/town_findings_voter_lists.json v001).

transcribes.work: Election Returns - Poll List of 1834, filed 11 August 1834
transcribes.note: 115 entries. Andreas independently dates the second town election to 11 August 1834, which corroborates the list's own heading.

85 entries. THE LIST PRINTS NO DATE, AND IT IS NOT THE POLL BOOK OF THE THIRD TOWN ELECTION. That election is now dated from the town's own newspaper rather than from Andreas: the Chicago Democrat of 8 July 1835 announced the election of Trustees under the new charter for 'Friday of this week' and the issue of 15 July reported that it 'took place on Friday last' with the return — FRIDAY 10 JULY 1835, nine days after the 1835-07-01 scene date (claims/town_election_1835_democrat.json d001-d005). Andreas's town chapter, 'in July, 1835', is corroborated; his police chapter's 5 August 1835 is the day the newly elected board sat and passed the town's ordinance code over Hugunin's name as President. But that return gives single candidates 124 and 142 votes, which 85 men cannot cast, and six of the ten men who stood are absent from these 85 while the list runs unbroken from Adams to Wright — so this is a DIFFERENT poll, not a short printing of that one (claims/town_findings_voter_lists.json v003). Which poll is open; the county and state general election of Monday 3 August 1835 is the nearest candidate. Until it is settled, a name here evidences presence in Chicago in 1835 and not presence on any particular day.

what_it_supplies: 345 names of men who voted at, or were taxed by, the Town of Chicago in 1833, 1834 and 1835, as printed
which of the four lists each name stands on, and its position in that list
the courtesy and rank titles the lists print in front of a name (Col., Lt., Major, Dr.)

for the 1835 poll list: presence in Chicago during 1835, which is the strongest residence evidence this project holds short of a newspaper naming the man — but NOT presence on a stated day, because the list is undated and is shown not to be the poll book of the 10 July 1835 town election (T-0542)
what_it_does_not_supply: any address, street, lot or dwelling
any age, trade, household or family member
any date more precise than a list's own heading — and the 1835 list has no heading date at all
any woman, and any man who neither voted nor was taxed

what_it_supplies: A name, a trade and a street for 1,655 entries in the city of 1839 — the closest address list to 1835 this project can reach.
A trade for 976 of them at a stated street, which compiles into 102 street faces (Lake 199, Clark 94, North Water 83, South Water 72).

On printed page 37: six churches with their ministers, fifteen hotels, the public offices around the Public Square, the land office, the lighthouse, the theatre, two named building rows, the Dutch Settlement, and the fire that took the Tremont House on 27 October 1839.
what_it_does_not_supply: An 1835 residency. Four years late, and the ratified ladder never makes a resident from a later listing alone.

An address number that means anything, off Lake street. Fergus writes on printed page 3 that no street but Lake was numbered in 1839 and that 'the numbers now given are those of the present day' — 1876's. Only the street name crosses.
A count of its own entries. The volume states no number of names anywhere, so a reading of it cannot be closed against the book the way a census sheet closes against its printed totals.

frontage.why: T-1622, the third deal on this block and the one that spends its last free business-front lot. THE FACE IS NOT RE-ARGUED: this block's north face is South Water Street, the town's business front, graded `principal` in the committed hierarchy, and the two runs already standing on this block — the first deal's on lot 6 and the second's on lot 2 — stand on its line at a 1.5 m setback. This run adopts the same setback, which is what puts its front wall on the line the block's other nine frontage roofs already stand on rather than on a line of its own. LOT 4 CAME OFF TWO OPEN-LOT LISTS TO BE DEALT THIS RUN, AND NEITHER OF THEM CALLED IT A RESERVED VACANCY. The first deal declared lots 4 and 6 as its frontage and stood its whole run on lot 6; T-1053 then listed lot 4 open, saying in its own words that it was held on the list "only because this parcel's privy stood in its yard" and that the privy had since moved to the lot it serves. The second deal repeated the listing with the same reason and added the only one it had of its own: "this deal was dealt the roofs it has built and asks the block for no more ground, so the lot stays open." Neither is the end-rule reading that makes lot 1 the block's open lot; both are a parcel saying it had no roof to put there. This deal has two, and they are two the platted seating asked this block for by name. So lot 4 leaves both lists and is built on, and lot 1 — the remotest lot from the bridge and the one the schedule's sizing reserves — is still open, which is the standard the density rule actually states. THE GROUND WAS MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS DEALT. Lot 4 projects onto the north face between 47.06 m and 72.12 m, so with the plat module's 1.5 m side margin the run has 22.06 m of buildable face. The nearest roof west of it is the second deal's two-room cottage recon_1835_blk_south_water_franklin_c2_08, whose east wall reads 46.21 m; the nearest east is the first deal's log dwelling recon_1835_blk_south_water_franklin_d1_04 at 77.13 m. Neither is touched: the run is anchored at the EAST end of its own frontage at the 1.5 m margin and packs back west, which leaves 6.51 m to d1_04 and better than eleven metres to d4_08, against a three-metre separation gate.
